The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 12, 2019
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 5:34 p.m. on March
12, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Wagner presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Christina Shea
  Mayor:  Donald P. Wagner

1.  CLOSED SESSION

  NOTE: Closed Session Items 1.1 - 1.4 were considered earlier in the
  day at a special City Council meeting. See 3 p.m. Special Meeting
  minutes.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Councilmember Fox led the Pledge of Allegiance.
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  INVOCATION

  Sheikh Atef Magoub, Religious Director of the Islamic Center of Irvine, provided the
  invocation.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Orange County Transportation Authority - Long Range Transportation
  Plan

  Mayor Wagner introduced Greg Nord, Principal Transportation Analyst, on
  behalf of Kia Mortazavi, Executive Director of Planning, Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA), who provided a brief update on OCTA’s
  long-range transportation plan.

  City Council discussion included: noting the importance of regional
  transportation as a whole; expressed support for additional bike lanes; and
  inquired about express toll lanes on California Interstate 405 (I-405) and its
  impacts, including costs and carpool fee waivers, to Irvine and Orange
  County residents.

  2.2  National Weather Service Storm Ready Recognition

  Mayor Wagner introduced staff from City of Irvine’s Public Safety’s Office of
  Emergency Management, Public Works, and Transportation Department;
  and Alex Tardy, Meteorologist, National Weather Service, who presented a
  certificate recognizing and declaring the City of Irvine as a “Storm Ready”
  City based on its collaborative efforts in select key areas and preparedness
  for weather-related emergencies.

  2.3  The Illumination Foundation

  Councilmember Khan introduced Paul Leon, CEO and Founding Officer,
  The Illumination Foundation, who provided an overview and video
  presentation of the services provided by the Foundation and expressed
  appreciation to the City Council for its continued support.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Russo provided a brief report on his trip to the United Kingdom,
  accompanied by Kaitlyn Nguyen, Manager of Economic Development, and introduced
  Linda DiMario, Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce, who provided a brief presentation
  highlighting key events that took place. Additionally, City Manager Russo provided a brief
  report on his recent trip to Sacramento, where he and Deputy City Manager Grettenberg
  met with the Governor’s staff, legislators, legislative staff, key departments, and other
  State officials to cover a number of priority areas for the City of Irvine; and noted his
  upcoming trip to Washington, D.C., where he and Deputy City Manager Grettenberg
  would address issues important to Irvine at the Federal level.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo noted that March 12, 2019 was “National Girl Scout Day” and
  encouraged community support of the Girl Scouts; acknowledged members of the Boy
  Scouts in attendance; and noted his recent attendance at the Woodbridge High School
  spring musical “Little Shop of Horrors.” He also announced two upcoming musicals,
  which included University High School’s “How to Succeed in Business Without Really
  Trying” March 14 – 16 at 7 p.m.; and Portola High School’s “Addams Family” March 14-
  16 at 7 p.m., and March 16 at 2 p.m.

  Councilmember Fox announced that the Irvine Community Land Trust was seeking an
  exemption/waiver of property taxes on projects during the construction process in order
  to avoid paying property taxes at market value on land designated for affordable
  housing.

  Mayor Pro Tempore Shea noted her recent attendance at “The Courage to Remember
  the Holocaust” exhibit at Irvine Valley College, which is on display through March 14.

  Mayor Wagner made the following announcements:

    For those who were unable to attend the first two Community Budget Meetings
  last week, two additional meetings will be held on Wednesday, March 13 from 6 to
  7 p.m. at Quail Hill Community Center; and Wednesday, March 20 from 6 to 7
  p.m. at Portola Springs Community Center. No RSVP is needed. For information,
  visit cityofirvine.org/budget.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

    The Irvine Animal Care Center invites the community to support its Foster
  Donation Drive taking place through March 31. Opportunities to support the
  center’s puppies, kittens, and young rabbits, as well as recuperating animals, are
  available through the donation of supplies such as formula, blankets, and toys. A
  complete wish list is available on the Irvine Animal Care Center’s website. In
  addition, anyone interested in volunteering with the center’s Foster Care Program,
  which provides shelter, supplies, food, and veterinary care for young animals and
  those recovering from medical procedures, can attend a Foster Volunteer
  Workshop on Sunday, March 24 from 1:30 to 4 p.m. by registering at
  yourirvine.org. For information, visit irvineanimals.org or call 949-724-7498.

    The spring issue of Inside Irvine is in homes, featuring stories on Great Park Ice,
  the City’s affordable housing efforts and transition to a two-year budget, and
  more. This edition also includes spring and summer camps, and classes for all
  interested ages. To register for camps and classes, visit yourirvine.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Fox, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Shea, and unanimously carried to approve City Council Consent
  Calendar Item Nos. 3.1 through 3.4, with the exception of Consent Calendar
  Item No. 3.2, which was removed for separate discussion.

  3.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City Council
  and regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine as Successor Agency
  to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency held on February 12,
  2019

  3.2  COMMENDATIONS

  This item was removed for separate discussion by Ilya Tseglin, Community
  Member, who spoke about Shir Ha-Ma’alot’s 50th Anniversary, as well as a
  domestic issue related to his autistic son.

  Mayor Wagner read excerpts from the proclamation and congratulated Shir
  Ha-Ma’alot on its 50th Anniversary.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4

  a. Irvine High Athletic Boosters Club Inc. ($400) (Contract

  b. Northwood High Athletic Boosters ($250) (Contract No.

  2)  Approved Councilmember Fox's request for Community Partnership

  4.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  4.1  REVIEW OF ENFORCEMENT STRATEGY FOR BOARDING HOUSES,
  AND SHORT-TERM RENTALS, AND CODE AMENDMENT TO CLARIFY
  THE DEFINITION OF “BOARDING HOUSE”

  Steve Holtz, Manager of Housing and Neighborhood Services, and Pete
  Carmichael, Director of Community Development, presented the staff
  report and responded to questions. Noam Duzman, Rutan & Tucker, was
  also available for questions.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  Prior to opening the public hearing, Mayor Wagner acknowledged
  correspondence received by members of the community and the
  commonality of concerns raised about discrimination based on familial
  status.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, clarified certain provisions under existing fair
  housing laws, as well as what was acceptable and prohibited under these
  laws.

  Mayor Wagner opened the public hearing at 6:48 p.m.

  Jeff Davis, Irvine Company, asked for clarification of the proposed
  ordinance and whether the definition of a “boarding house” would apply to
  its Student Housing Program.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the ordinance:

  Mario Lopez, Irvine Association Services
  Hoan Vo, Irvine resident
  Jane Olinger, Irvine resident
  Kamaran Nouri, Irvine resident
  Steve Lynch, Irvine resident
  Scott Couchman, Irvine resident
  Andy Zelinko, Irvine resident

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the ordinance:

  Davida Gregory, Irvine resident
  Sherry Avella, Irvine resident
  Mahamoud Elfarrah, Mission Viejo resident
  Cassius Rutherford, Costa Mesa resident
  Mark Richard Daniels, Anaheim resident
  R. Joshua Collins, Irvine resident
  Ashley Alvarez, Irvine resident
  Theresa Loveless, Irvine resident
  Annie Le, Irvine resident
  Jeanne Le, Irvine resident
  Jacobus Kos, Irvine resident
  Elizabeth Donaldson, Irvine resident
  Susan Sayre, Irvine resident
  Izzak Morales, Irvine resident
  Courtney Santos, Irvine resident
  Hans Kraus, Irvine resident
  Deyania Nevarez Martinez, Irvine resident
  Richard Prince
  David McCullagh, Irvine resident

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  Ken Stahl, Irvine resident
  Azniv Derdzakyan, Irvine resident
  Juta Gamboa, Irvine resident
  Rebecca Whitehead, Irvine resident
  Olivia Ramacier, Irvine resident
  Brigitte
  Matthew Downing, Irvine resident

  The following individuals submitted a Request to Speak but did not speak:

  Timothy Houcher
  David
  Kev Abazajian
  Jasmine

  By consensus, Mayor Wagner closed the public hearing at 8:20 p.m.

  City Council discussion included: addressing existing concerns raised by
  the student and senior populations and exploring solutions; expressed
  concern about increasing attendance over the years at University of
  California, Irvine (UCI) and impacts to surrounding neighborhoods and
  infrastructure; clarified the intent of the proposed ordinance; expressed
  concern about the City playing a role in determining housing types and
  family units; inquired about remedies for code enforcement violations and
  noted that stronger enforcement was necessary; questioned the use of a
  consultant for purposes of identifying short-term rentals and associated
  costs; suggested formation of a working committee with the Mayor, City
  staff, and representatives from the Irvine Company and FivePoint
  Communities, to meet with University of California, Irvine representatives to
  discuss affordable housing needs for students; questioned whether
  investigative and other costs were recoverable in court; questioned the
  need for defining a “Single Housekeeping Unit” and suggested removal of
  the definition from the proposed ordinance; and discussed balancing
  quality of life with legal challenges.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor  Pro Tempore  Shea, seconded  by
  Councilmember Kuo, to:

  Create a working group, consisting of two to four meetings,
  comprised of the City Manager, the Mayor, staff, representatives
  from the Irvine Company, and representatives from FivePoint
  Communities to meet with representatives from the University of
  California, Irvine, to begin a conversation to aggressively explore
  appropriate housing for students on campus.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  Following discussion related to adding a member of the Irvine Community
  Land Trust to the committee, Mayor Pro Tempore Shea amended her
  motion.

  ACTION:  An amendment to the motion was made by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Shea, and accepted by Councilmember Kuo as the
  seconder, and unanimously carried to:

  Create a working group, consisting of two to four meetings,
  comprised of the City Manager, the Mayor, staff, representatives
  from the Irvine Company, and representatives from FivePoint
  Communities to meet with representatives from the University of
  California, Irvine, to begin a conversation to aggressively explore
  appropriate housing for students on campus as amended to include
  a member of the City Council who also serves on the Irvine
  Community Land Trust Board.

  Wagner

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  Mayor Wagner left the meeting at 8:56 p.m.

 City Council Minutes  March 12, 2019

  5.3  CONSIDERATION  OF  COUNCILMEMBER  KUO'S  REQUEST
  REGARDING NATIONAL VOLUNTEER WEEK AND 1,000,000 HOUR
  CHALLENGE

  This item was agendized at the request of Councilmember Kuo, who noted
  the importance of volunteering, and suggested several options for residents
  to get involved in the community.

  City Council discussion included: creating a large “thermometer” or
  something similar on the City’s website and at City Hall to record the
  progress made with respect to the number of volunteer hours; expressed
  concern about the amount of staff time required to implement the
  Challenge; reiterated the list of nonprofit organizations on the City’s
  website for those seeking volunteer opportunities; and inquired about any
  rewards or prizes should the 1,000,000 hour goal be reached.

  Jimmee Medina, Director of Human Resources and Innovation, presented
  an example of a smartphone application used by Boston University that
  records the progress of volunteer hours provided by members of the
  community.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Shea, and unanimously carried by those members present
  (Mayor Wagner absent), to:

  1)  Proclaim April 7-13, 2019 as “National Volunteer Week.”
  2)  Issue a challenge to residents of the City of Irvine to volunteer
  1,000,000 hours of community service.
  3)  Direct staff to implement an online format to record and display
  the progress of the Challenge.
  4)  Direct staff to coordinate a method for individuals and groups
  in Irvine to be able to contact organizations seeking volunteer
  assistance.
